title: Machine learning prediction of PICC-associated thrombotic complications in critically ill patients.
summary: primary Methods/Results document the AI-enabled result, evaluation and bounded interpretation.
ai_technology: Random Forest and four comparator machine-learning models

evidence.tested: Five models were trained on 8,145 PICC insertions from 6,376 MIMIC-IV patients. Random Forest had AUC 0.809 (95% CI 0.780–0.838); patient-clustered splitting reduced AUC to 0.696, indicating within-patient correlation affected the primary split.
evidence.unknown: The reported evaluation does not establish prospective benefit or performance beyond the studied setting.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts PICC-associated thrombosis from clinical variables in MIMIC-IV; Random Forest was the best of five evaluated models.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
